newsitem.title: FRANCE: Jospin says Madelin-Seguin ticket anti-European.
newsitem.headline: Jospin says Madelin-Seguin ticket anti-European.

text.p: French Socialist leader Lionel Jospin said on Thursday that any new centre-right government with former finance minister Alain Madelin and National Assembly speaker Philippe Seguin at the helm would be bad for social policy and anti-European.
"An impossible couple. The least social and the most anti-European," he told reporters during a campaign walkabout.

Seguin, who campaigned against the Maastricht treaty in a 1992 referendum, and Madelin, who favours fast free market reforms, have been pushed to the forefront of the centre-right's campaign ahead of the second round of voting on Sunday in France's parliamentary election.

Seguin has since said he respects France's referendum vote in favour of economic and monetary union, but hopes the EMU "straitjacket" will be loosened after 1999 once German public support has been won.
Seguin and Madelin's prominence in the campaign has fuelled speculation that the former could become prime minister and the latter finance minister in the event of a centre-right victory.
